title: Measuring Laplace pressure and imaging the actin cortex during cytokinesis in cultured cells
protocol: Disassociate HeLa cells as described in steps 3d - 3g of the Cell culture section.
Plate disassociated HeLa cells in glass-bottom Petri dishes.
Incubate plated cells in a humidified 37°C, 5% CO2 incubator for 24 h to reach about 50–60% confluency as observed by light microscopy.
Rinse HeLa cells 2–3 times with prewarmed PBS to wash away nonadherent cells and debris.
Add 2 ml fresh complete culture medium after rinsing, then incubate in a CO2 incubator for 2–3 h.
Make micropipette from borosilicate glass capillary tubes using the micropipette puller and microforge as described.
Mount the prepared micropipette onto the pipette holder that allows fine control of the pipette movements in three dimensions.
Stretch the micropipette from a glass capillary using a micropipette puller in two-stage pull mode.
Cut the taper of the pulled micropipette at the desired micropipette radius by placing it against a hot metal wire.
Polish the end of the micropipette by bringing it close to the heated bead to remove sharp edges.
Place the micropipette in the micropipette puller.
Adjust the position so that its tip protrudes about 5 mm beyond the heating elements.
Heat up the tip and bend it using another micropipette to an angle of 35–40 degrees.
Passivate the micropipette with a β-casein solution (optional).
Ensure the micropipette tip is smooth for a good seal to the plasma membrane.
Keep the length of the bent part of the micropipette tip as short as possible, ideally 5-8 mm.
Avoid touching the tip when handling to prevent breakage and potential injury.
Store the fabricated micropipettes in a dust-free container (optional).
Prepare extra micropipettes on the day of the experiment if no storage is available.
Prepare a solution composed of 70% PBS and 30% FBS (10 mL).
Immerse the micropipette tip in the solution until it fills by capillary action.
Backfill the shank of the micropipette using a microelectrode filling needle and a syringe until a hemisphere droplet forms at the back end.
Ensure there are no air bubbles in the micropipette during backfilling.
Mount the micropipette onto the pipette holder.
Dismount the pipette holder from micromanipulator and take it out from the living cell workstation.
Position the pipette holder so that its outlet is flush with the liquid level in the water reservoirs.
Switch hand valves #1 and #2 to connect the micropipette holder to one of the water reservoirs.
Loosen the micropipette holder tip and squeeze out a hemispherical water droplet at the holder outlet by slowly lowering the height of the micropipette holder.
Insert the micropipette into the micropipette holder, and tighten the micropipette holder to ensure firm grip and good sealing.
Wipe off any excess fluid.
Make sure that there are no air bubbles trapped during the micropipette installation.
Do not tighten the knob of micropipette holder too much to avoid breaking the micropipette.
Remount the micropipette holder onto the micromanipulator.
Ensure that the micropipette holder is tightly clamped to reduce fluctuations of the micropipette during the experiment.
Control hand valves #1 and #2 to prevent water from flowing out before remounting the micropipette holder.
Heat up the tip of the micropipette with spiral-shaped heating elements.
Bend the heated tip to a required angle using another obsolete micropipette.
Fill the micropipette until a hemisphere droplet is formed at the back end.
Insert the micropipette into the micropipette holder.
Assemble components including micropipette holder, micropipette, and connecting tubing.
Move the micropipette tip into the center of the field of view.
Focus on the tip of the micropipette.
Calibrate the micropipette aspiration system to ensure a null-pressure condition when the micropipette tip contacts with the cell surface.
Locate the micropipette in the microscope field.
Turn on the anti-vibration table.
Put the culture dish with HeLa cells on the stage of the microscope.
Observe using the 10× objective in phase contrast mode.
Adjust the angle (40–45 degrees) of the pipette holder to ensure the micropipette tip is positioned approximately parallel to the bottom of the plate.
Bring the micropipette to a safe distance above the culture dish and into the field of view using the coarse adjustment on the micromanipulator.
Set this reference point as the home position and store this position on the micromanipulator keyboard.
Slowly bring down the micropipette until it enters the culture medium.
Use the micromanipulator in fine adjustment mode to lower the tip to a point just above the cell layer (50–100 μm).
Move the micropipette tip to the center of microscope field.
Once the micropipette tip is immersed into the culture medium, use the fine adjustment on the micromanipulator to lower the tip to minimize the potential for breaking it on the bottom of the dish.
Set this reference point as the target position, and store this position on the micromanipulator keyboard.
Check the micropipette.
Focus on the micropipette tip by adjusting the 10× objective.
Switch the hand valves #1 and #2 to connect a water reservoir #1 to the micropipette.
Apply pressure (e.g., 1,000 Pa) to the micropipette by raising the water reservoir to check whether the tip is blocked, damaged or poorly polished.
Ensure the pressure is large enough to form a conical-shaped jet at the micropipette tip.
Check for damage or poor polishing of the micropipette tip by observing changes in the shape of the jet.
Alternatively, switch the objective to higher magnification (e.g., 100×) to check for damage on the micropipette tip.
Return the water reservoir #1 to its original position after inspection.
Add 25 μL polystyrene microbeads diluted 1 : 400 in filtered sterilized water to the culture dish.
Carefully move and position the micropipette tip next to a suspended microbead.
Switch hand valve #1 to connect the water reservoir #2 to both water reservoir #1 and micropipette.
Adjust the height of the water reservoir #1 so that this microbead does not move toward or away from the micropipette tip.
Switch the hand valve #1 so that only the water reservoir #2 connects to the micropipette after calibrating the micropipette aspiration system.
Calibrate the micropipette aspiration system before each experiment.
Observe the shape of the jet at the micropipette tip directly.
Scrutinize the micropipette tip closely with higher-magnification objective.
Measure the Laplace pressure of HeLa cells undergoing cytokinesis in media with different osmolarities using micropipette aspiration.

Determine the Laplace pressure of cytokinetic cells incubated in hypotonic, isotonic or hypertonic medium by virtue of the micropipette aspiration experiment, image and data analysis, as well as the medium replacement device.
Prepare experimental media with different osmolarities for hypotonic, isotonic, and hypertonic conditions.

Determine the mass of sucrose required for solutions with osmolarities of 120, 210, 300, 390, and 480 mOsm/L using the equation: mass of solute = molar mass × moles of solute, where molarity = moles of solute / liter of solution.
Weigh out sucrose of required mass into a beaker.
Pour 500 ml of deionized water into the beaker and dissolve sucrose using a magnetic stirrer.
Transfer the sucrose solution into a 1L graduated cylinder and fill to the 1L mark with deionized water.
Pour the solution back into the beaker for full agitation before storage.
Mix sucrose solutions with isotonic culture medium in a ratio of 2 : 1.
Establish media at osmolalities of 180 mOsm/L, 240 mOsm/L, 300 mOsm/L, 360 mOsm/L, and 420 mOsm/L.
Perform the micropipette aspiration experiment.
Start up the displacement measurement system with a laser displacement sensor, data acquisition card, and computer.
Shift the micropipette to the home position using the micromanipulator.
Place a new culture dish with HeLa cells on the microscope stage.
Cover the culture dish with the cut lid of the medium replacement device.
Find a round-shaped (M phase) HeLa cell with visible chromosomes on the equatorial plate.
Place the identified cell in the center of the visual field.
Position the micropipette to the target position using the micromanipulator.
Switch to the 100× oil-immersion objective.
Add a drop of immersion oil on the 100× objective before switching.
Slowly move the micropipette until its tip gently touches the cell membrane.
Grab the cell by applying suction with the water reservoir #2 when it starts forming cleavage furrow and enters cytokinesis.
Gently adjust the position of the water reservoir during the micropipette aspiration experiment.
Increase the suction pressure stepwise by changing the position of the water reservoir #2 until it reaches a critical value Pc.
Start imaging and record the displacement of the water reservoir #2 at the same time.
Fill the syringe #1 of the medium replacement device with prewarmed hypotonic, isotonic or hypertonic media (37°C) as required.
Prewarm hypotonic and hypertonic media to 37°C in a water bath kettle.
Pump out original medium using syringe #2.
Inject the prewarmed hypotonic, isotonic, or hypertonic medium with syringe #1 as required.
Adjust suction pressure to maintain the aspirated part of the cell roughly hemispherical during media exchange and cytokinesis.
Rapidly complete media exchange within 20 seconds.
Release the cell when contractile-ring contraction is complete.
Shift micropipette to home position.
Repeat steps c–m for other cells undergoing cytokinesis.
Replace cell culture dish after each aspiration experiment.
Replace medium in syringe #1 with fresh, prewarmed medium before each new experiment.
Disconnect two water reservoirs from the micropipette using hand valve #1 post-experiment.
Unmount and empty the micropipette after disconnecting.
Calculate cortical tension and Laplace pressure.
Open images using ImageJ software.
Set scale to micrometers using the Set Scale command in ImageJ.
Measure radius Rp of the micropipette.
Measure radius Rc of curvature at the interface in contact with micropipette.
Retrieve displacement data of water reservoir #2.
Calculate critical pressure Pc corresponding to each image processed with ImageJ.
Ensure points in time for processed images and retrieved displacement data are the same.
Calculate cortical tension from Laplace equation Tc = Pc / [2(1/Rp – 1/Rc)].
Calculate Laplace pressure of the cell undergoing cytokinesis using PL = 2 Tc / Rc.
Image actin cortex for cells undergoing cytokinesis in media with different osmolarities.
Transfect HeLa cells with Lifeact-GFP plasmid.
Analyze cortex density distribution of cytokinetic cells incubated in hypotonic, isotonic or hypertonic medium.
Seed 5 × 10^5 to 6 × 10^5 HeLa cells per glass-bottom Petri dish in 2 mL of complete growth medium.
Incubate cells overnight in a humidified 37°C, 7% CO2 incubator.
Mix 125 μL Opti-MEM® medium with 2.5 μg Lifeact-GFP plasmid and 4 μL Lipo8000TM transfection reagent according to the manufacturer’s instructions.
Transfect cells with the mixture prepared in step b.
Culture cells for 24–36 hours after transfection.
Verify transfection efficiency using a fluorescence microscope.
Rinse transfected HeLa cells 2–3 times with prewarmed PBS.
Add fresh complete culture medium and incubate at 37°C (5% CO2) for 2–3 h.
Find a round-shaped (M phase) transfected HeLa cell using the 10× objective and place it in the center of the visual field.
Switch to the 100× oil-immersion objective.
Start imaging in bright field, green channel when the cell begins cytokinesis.
Regulate exposure time and light intensity to reduce fluorescence quenching.
Exchange media during imaging.
Stop imaging when contractile-ring contraction completes.
Repeat steps to open fluorescent images using ImageJ.
Select the Freehand Line (line width 10 pixels) and trace HeLa cell contour.
Go to Analyze → Plot Profile from the main menu to quantify the intensity distribution along the cell contour.
Go to Data → Save Data from the plot to save the experiment data for further analysis using ORIGINPRO® 2021b.
